evals.name: audit-and-rewrite-claude-md
evals.prompt: I wrote this CLAUDE.md for a Python project a while back and Claude seems to ignore half of it. Can you audit it and rewrite it to work well on Opus 4.7?
evals.expected_output: Structured audit + rewrite: CLAUDE.md under 200 lines, negatives flipped to positives, shouting dialed back, deprecated params removed, {date} cache-breaker handled, self-evident filler cut, motivation added to non-obvious rules.

assertions.name: Audit report present
assertions.check: Output contains a structured audit with rubric categories (directness/framing/structure/type-specific)

assertions.name: Rewritten file under 200 lines
assertions.check: The rewritten CLAUDE.md file is under 200 lines

assertions.name: Deprecated params removed
assertions.check: Rewritten prompt does not mention 'budget_tokens' or 'temperature=0' (either removed or replaced with adaptive thinking / effort guidance)

assertions.name: Shouting dialed back
assertions.check: Rewritten prompt has fewer than 3 instances of all-caps shouting words (CRITICAL/NEVER/MUST/ALWAYS/ABSOLUTELY) compared to original's 20+

assertions.name: Negatives reduced
assertions.check: Ratio of negative constructions ('Don't', 'NEVER', 'avoid') to positive imperatives is meaningfully lower in rewrite vs original

assertions.name: Self-evident filler cut
assertions.check: Rewrite does not contain 'Be helpful', 'Be accurate', 'Think carefully', 'Write clean code' (all present in original)

assertions.name: Cache invalidator handled
assertions.check: The {date} interpolation from original is either removed, explained, or noted — not copied verbatim

assertions.name: Changelog present
assertions.check: Report includes a changelog mapping changes to rubric items or principles

evals.name: audit-and-rewrite-agent
evals.prompt: Review this Claude Code agent definition and tell me what's wrong with it, then rewrite it so it actually triggers correctly and performs well.
evals.expected_output: Audit flags vague description, missing examples, tool bloat, shouting, deprecated params, filler rules. Rewrite has specific description, 2-3 <example> blocks, trimmed tools.

assertions.name: Audit flags vague description
assertions.check: Audit explicitly identifies the description ('A powerful assistant') as too vague to trigger correctly

assertions.name: Audit flags missing examples
assertions.check: Audit identifies that the agent lacks <example> blocks (whenToUse) which are the primary triggering mechanism

assertions.name: Audit flags tool bloat
assertions.check: Audit questions whether WebSearch/WebFetch/Task are needed for a code-helper agent

assertions.name: Rewrite has specific description
assertions.check: Rewritten description includes specific trigger phrases and when-to-use context, not just 'a powerful assistant'

assertions.name: Rewrite has example blocks
assertions.check: Rewritten agent has at least 2 <example> blocks in whenToUse

assertions.name: Deprecated params removed
assertions.check: Rewritten agent does not mention budget_tokens or temperature=0

assertions.name: Shouting reduced
assertions.check: Rewritten agent has fewer than 3 instances of CRITICAL/MUST/NEVER/ALWAYS/ABSOLUTELY

evals.name: audit-jinja-caching
evals.prompt: We're using this Jinja2 template as the system prompt for a caching-enabled Anthropic API app, but our cache hit rate is basically zero. Can you audit it? Do not rewrite yet — just tell me what's broken.
evals.expected_output: Audit-only output identifying silent cache invalidators in the cached region and rubric failures specific to Jinja2 templates.

assertions.name: Identifies now() as cache breaker
assertions.check: Audit explicitly calls out {{ now() }} or {{ now().strftime(...) }} as a per-request cache invalidator

assertions.name: Identifies session_id/request_id as cache breakers
assertions.check: Audit calls out session_id, request_id, or user.id appearing early in the template as invalidators

assertions.name: Identifies session history iteration
assertions.check: Audit notes that {% for q in session.history %} changes per-request and invalidates cache

assertions.name: Identifies iteration ordering risk
assertions.check: Audit notes that iterating over user.enabled_features (possibly unordered set) or available_tools can produce non-deterministic output

assertions.name: No rewrite produced
assertions.check: Output stays in audit mode — does not produce a full rewritten template

assertions.name: Flags shouting
assertions.check: Audit identifies 'ALWAYS'/'NEVER'/'MUST' as over-triggering language

assertions.name: Structured rubric output
assertions.check: Audit uses the rubric categories (or equivalent structured scoring), not just prose

evals.name: rewrite-zod-tools
evals.prompt: These Zod tool descriptions are way too terse and the model keeps picking the wrong tool. Rewrite them per Opus 4.7 best practices.
evals.expected_output: Each tool description answers what/when/params. Parameter descriptions are specific. Filler removed. Length stays short (1-3 sentences per tool).

assertions.name: Tool descriptions answer when-to-use
assertions.check: Rewritten descriptions include 'when' context (disambiguating from other tools), not just 'what the tool does'

assertions.name: Parameter descriptions specific
assertions.check: Rewritten parameter descriptions are longer than one word and describe purpose or example values

assertions.name: Enum values explained
assertions.check: Rewritten create_item sort/type enums and delete_item force parameter have semantic meaning explained

assertions.name: Filler removed
assertions.check: Rewrite does not contain 'A function that' or 'This function is used to' constructions

assertions.name: Stays concise
assertions.check: Each tool description is 1-3 sentences — not bloated into paragraphs

assertions.name: Valid TypeScript
assertions.check: Rewritten .ts file is syntactically valid TypeScript (parseable imports, valid z.object syntax)

evals.name: audit-and-rewrite-system-prompt
evals.prompt: Here's a system prompt I drafted for a customer support bot. Audit it and improve it.
evals.expected_output: Audit catches shouting, deprecated params, guess-and-ship anti-pattern, friendly/upsell tension. Rewrite fixes these.

assertions.name: Audit flags deprecated params
assertions.check: Audit identifies budget_tokens and/or temperature=0 as deprecated/removed on Opus 4.7

assertions.name: Audit flags guess anti-pattern
assertions.check: Audit identifies 'just make your best guess' as problematic (teaches hallucination)

assertions.name: Audit identifies tension
assertions.check: Audit notes the tension between 'be friendly/professional' and 'try to upsell'

assertions.name: Rewrite removes guess-and-ship
assertions.check: Rewritten prompt replaces 'make your best guess' with 'ask the user' or 'say you don't know'

assertions.name: Rewrite removes deprecated params
assertions.check: Rewritten prompt does not mention budget_tokens or temperature

assertions.name: Shouting reduced
assertions.check: Rewritten prompt has fewer than 3 instances of CRITICAL/MUST/NEVER/ALWAYS/ABSOLUTELY

assertions.name: Changelog present
assertions.check: Report includes a changelog showing what changed and why
